results.title: Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
results.summary: Formalizes the 'fleet-memory problem' for cooperating LLM agents and proposes systems primitives (scoped retrieval, temporal supersession, provenance tracking, policy-governed propagation) implemented in the MemClaw reference system, evaluated via the ArgusFleet harness.

results.title: Multi-Agent Memory from a Computer Architecture Perspective: Visions and Challenges Ahead
results.summary: Frames multi-agent LLM memory through classical computer architecture, contrasting shared vs. distributed memory prototypes, proposing an Agent I/O/Cache/Memory hierarchy, and identifying memory consistency and cross-agent cache-sharing protocols as the key open gaps.

results.title: Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads
results.summary: First systems characterization of agent memory: introduces a four-axis taxonomy, a phase-aware profiling harness, evaluates ten representative systems, and derives system recommendations including fleet-scale management and freshness-latency tradeoffs.

results.title: Oracle Agent Memory as an Enterprise Memory Substrate for Long-Horizon AI Agents
results.summary: Proposes a database-native memory substrate built on Oracle Database, with a layered architecture separating an active memory core from a passive store interface; reports 93.8% accuracy on LongMemEval using ~10.7x fewer tokens than flat-history baselines.

results.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
results.summary: Dual-granularity context management framework (Ingestion-Aware Compaction + Lifecycle-Aware Eviction) that preserves prompt-cache continuity for long agent sessions, reducing inference cost 56-87% on PinchBench and Claw-Eval; integrated into LightMem2 with open-source code.

results.title: Agent Memory Below the Prompt: Persistent Q4 KV Cache for Multi-Agent LLM Inference on Edge Devices
results.summary: Persists per-agent KV caches to disk in 4-bit quantization and reloads them directly into attention layers, fitting 4x more agent contexts into a fixed RAM budget and cutting time-to-first-token by up to 136x for multi-agent inference on constrained/edge nodes.

results.title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
results.summary: Systematic experimental study treating agent memory as a data management system, decomposing it into representation/storage, extraction, retrieval/routing, and maintenance modules, and benchmarking 12 memory systems across 11 datasets to expose operational cost and architectural tradeoffs.

results.title: Multi-Agent Systems Have a Distributed Systems Problem
results.summary: Argues that multi-agent LLM systems inherit classical distributed-systems challenges (Byzantine fault tolerance, consistency, coordination) and that agent memory and messaging must be designed with these guarantees rather than treated as isolated per-agent state.
